# Temple Scroll Column 51 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 51 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**51:1** You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep straying and ignore them; you shall surely return them to your brother.

**51:2** And if your brother is not nearby, or you do not know who he is, then you shall bring it into your house, and it shall remain with you until your brother inquires after it, and you shall restore it to him.

**51:3** And so you shall do with his donkey, and so you shall do with his garment, and so you shall do with every lost item of your brother's that is lost from him and that you find; you may not ignore it.

**51:4** You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road and ignore them; you shall surely help him raise it up.

**51:5** A woman shall not wear a man's garment, nor shall a man put on a woman's clothing; for everyone who does these things is an abomination to the LORD your God.

**51:6** If a bird's nest happens to be before you along the way, in any tree or on the ground, with young birds or eggs, and the mother is sitting upon the young or upon the eggs, you shall not take the mother together with the offspring.

**51:7** You shall surely send the mother away, but the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may prolong your days.

**51:8** When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring blood-guilt upon your house if someone falls from it.

**51:9** You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, lest the whole yield become forfeited — both the seed that you sow and the produce of the vineyard.

**51:10** You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.

**51:11** You shall not wear a garment of mixed fabric, wool and linen woven together.

**51:12** You shall make tassels for yourself on the four corners of the cloak with which you cover yourself.

**51:13** If a man takes a wife and goes in to her and then comes to hate her,

**51:14** and brings charges of misconduct against her and gives her an evil name, saying: I took this woman, and when I approached her I did not find in her the tokens of virginity —

**51:15** then the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring forth the tokens of the young woman's virginity before the elders of the city at the gate.

**51:16** And the father of the young woman shall say to the elders: I gave my daughter to this man as a wife, and he has come to hate her.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 51 reworks Deuteronomy 22:1-17 in the divine first-person voice characteristic of the Temple Scroll. "Tokens of virginity" follows standard scholarly convention for betulim. "Tassels" for gedilim (cf. Deut 22:12). "Mixed fabric" for sha'atnez. The legislation moves from property laws through miscellaneous regulations to marriage law.*
